goal: Establish actual current behavior before changes, prove submission safety, and create a regression baseline.

items.instr:
Audit src/applications/, src/profile/, src/leads/, src/scout/, src/astro/.
Trace lead → qualification → preparation → approval → submission → tracking → outcome → learning.
Verify runtime/code paths; document implemented, stubbed and partially wired behavior.
Create a repeatable regression baseline.
items.doneWhen: Current behavior and gaps are documented and baseline tests pass.

items.instr:
Audit email, ATS/browser, portal, retry, prepared/queued and scheduled autonomous paths.
Low-level submission functions must independently enforce sandbox/kill-switch checks.
Fail closed; never bypass CAPTCHA, authentication or access controls.
items.doneWhen: Every real submission path is blocked whenever safety conditions require it, including direct low-level invocation.

items.instr: Cover ingestion, deduplication, profile validation, scoring, CV generation, email/portal preparation, approval, retries, inbox tracking and learning infrastructure.
items.doneWhen: Automated baseline tests pass.

goal: Replace ad-hoc match scoring with a single qualification engine and hard eligibility checks.

items.instr:
Evaluate profile, normalized job, eligibility, evidence, job quality, career fit and application/channel information.
Return QUALIFIED, CONDITIONAL, NEAR_MISS, REJECT or INSUFFICIENT_DATA plus score, confidence, reasons, blockers and missing information.
Downstream channels consume the central result.
items.doneWhen: Qualification is deterministic/replayable and downstream selection uses it.

items.instr:
Evaluate location, authorization where known, employment type, seniority, mandatory experience/skills, education/certification where genuinely required, salary, notice period and language.
Distinguish HARD_FAIL from UNKNOWN; never guess material facts.
items.doneWhen: Mandatory requirements are independently evaluated with evidence or explicit UNKNOWN.

items.instr:
Extract role, seniority, must-have/preferred skills, responsibilities, experience, location/remote rules, employment type, compensation, authorization, notice/start requirements, technology/domain, channel, employer and freshness.
Preserve original JD evidence and separate explicit requirements from inference.
items.doneWhen: Same JD produces a stable representation traceable to source text or labelled inference.

items.instr:
Use work history, projects, education, skills, CV, portfolio, GitHub and verified profile data.
Every material match needs evidence; never manufacture experience, employers, achievements, metrics, technologies or certifications.
items.doneWhen: Material matches are explainable using candidate evidence.

items.instr:
Support synonyms, aliases, related technologies and framework/library relationships.
Avoid false equivalence such as Java vs JavaScript.
Retain explainability.
items.doneWhen: Recall improves without materially increasing false-positive skill matches.

items.instr:
Classify NONE, MINOR, MODERATE, MAJOR, BLOCKING and UNKNOWN.
Consider must-have/preferred status, transferable skills, seniority and related technologies.
Never hide a genuine blocker.
items.doneWhen: Gap classification is deterministic, explainable and used by qualification.

goal: Add career-fit, job-quality and ROI scoring plus explainable decisions.

items.instr:
Evaluate trajectory, seniority, technology direction, domain, compensation, location and stability.
Distinguish technical match from good career match.
items.doneWhen: Career fit explicitly contributes to the decision.

items.instr:
Evaluate posting age, availability, employer signals, duplicates, stale/reposted listings and closing/deadline information.
Downgrade low-quality jobs even when candidate fit is strong.
items.doneWhen: Quality/freshness affects ranking and stale/closed jobs are safely excluded.

items.instr:
Consider qualification probability, job quality, channel success probability, effort, response likelihood and tailoring cost.
Do not optimize solely for application count.
items.doneWhen: Ranking incorporates expected value, not only match score.

items.instr:
Show decision, score, confidence, strongest matches, gaps, blockers, uncertainty, expected value, channel and CV strategy.
Provide evidence/source references where possible.
items.doneWhen: Operator can understand the decision without reading model internals.

items.instr:
Identify preferred-skill gaps, related technology, title differences, modest experience mismatch or resolvable missing information.
Never override genuine hard blockers; route near misses separately.
items.doneWhen: Near misses are separately identified and never silently treated as fully qualified.

goal: Ground CV generation in a verified evidence library with drift protection and dual ATS/human scoring.

items.instr:
Store skills, employment, projects, education, certifications, achievements, links, dates and locations.
Track source, confidence, verification status and version/date.
items.doneWhen: Tailoring retrieves facts from the evidence layer.

items.instr:
Choose based on role, seniority, JD emphasis, domain, geography, ATS needs and evidence.
Examples: backend, full-stack, AI/automation, management, domain-specific.
Variants must not contain contradictory facts.
items.doneWhen: Strategy is selected systematically and recorded.

items.instr:
Tailor summary, skill ordering, projects, experience emphasis and terminology.
Every material claim maps to candidate evidence.
items.doneWhen: Generated CVs pass automated evidence validation.

items.instr:
Compare tailored CV with master evidence.
Detect invented skills, inflated experience, changed dates, unsupported metrics, altered titles and unsupported responsibilities.
Reject or flag excessive drift.
items.doneWhen: Unsupported material claims reliably fail validation.

items.instr:
Evaluate keyword coverage, semantic relevance, readability, structure, evidence strength and keyword stuffing.
Do not insert irrelevant keywords merely to increase ATS score.
items.doneWhen: Separate ATS and human-relevance signals are available.

goal: Make channel selection, ATS question handling, browser field mapping and deduplication smarter and learnable.

items.instr:
Track ATS, direct HR email, recruiter, easy apply and portal outcomes.
Control for job quality and candidate fit.
items.doneWhen: Historical channel performance affects future channel selection.

items.instr:
Detect unknown, conditional, dropdown, radio, multi-select and free-text fields.
Answer only from verified evidence; stop/ask/flag for unknown or high-risk questions.
Never guess legal/demographic/authorization information.
items.doneWhen: Unknown questions cannot silently receive fabricated answers.

items.instr:
Learn common field mappings and store by portal/form signature.
Revalidate when form structure changes.
items.doneWhen: Known forms populate reliably and changed forms trigger re-validation.

items.instr:
Use employer, normalized title, location, JD similarity, external IDs, canonical URL and posting identity.
Distinguish genuine reposts from separate vacancies.
items.doneWhen: Equivalent jobs resolve to one canonical opportunity.

goal: Improve decisions using employer-specific signals, recruiter context and outcome-driven learning.

items.instr:
Track employer identity/domain, ATS, channel, response behavior, outcomes and repost patterns.
Use evidence-backed signals; do not create an unverified blacklist.
items.doneWhen: Employer information safely influences decisions.

items.instr:
Track recruiter, employer, roles, contact history and responses.
Avoid duplicate outreach and respect retention/privacy.
items.doneWhen: Future applications can recognize prior recruiter relationships.

items.instr:
Record rejection stage, channel, role, qualification, CV strategy, timing, employer and known reason.
Use aggregate evidence; one rejection must not create a rule.
items.doneWhen: Rejection outcomes update controlled learning features.

items.instr: Track interviews, stages, offers, accepted/rejected offers, role, channel, CV strategy and employer.
items.doneWhen: Positive outcomes demonstrably feed future scoring.

items.instr:
Compare predicted confidence with outcomes; track calibration, false positives, false negatives and uncertainty.
Do not treat confidence as probability until empirically calibrated.
items.doneWhen: Calibration metrics are available and monitored.

goal: Track and learn from template and CV strategy variants.

items.instr:
Version emails, recruiter messages, cover letters and CV strategies.
Record the version with every application.
items.doneWhen: Every application is traceable to its exact content version.

items.instr:
Compare response, interview, offer and rejection rates.
Control for job quality/fit and avoid conclusions from tiny samples.
items.doneWhen: Template performance is measurable and responsibly interpreted.

items.instr:
Track outcomes by strategy, role, industry, seniority and channel.
Make learning reversible and auditable.
items.doneWhen: Future strategy selection uses measured historical performance.

goal: Create one authoritative application lifecycle with safe portal polling and follow-up automation.

items.instr:
Define states such as DISCOVERED, QUALIFIED, CONDITIONAL, PREPARED, AWAITING_APPROVAL, APPROVED, SUBMITTED, DELIVERED, IN_REVIEW, INTERVIEW, OFFER, REJECTED, WITHDRAWN and FAILED.
Define valid transitions and prevent impossible transitions.
items.doneWhen: Applications follow a validated lifecycle.

items.instr:
Poll supported portals safely; preserve evidence/timestamps; handle login failures and back off on errors.
Never bypass access controls.
items.doneWhen: Supported portals update lifecycle status reliably.

items.instr:
Consider application date, channel, employer, response status, recruiter relationship and prior communication.
Never follow up after rejection/withdrawal; respect caps and approval/sandbox controls.
items.doneWhen: Follow-ups are lifecycle-aware, deduplicated and safety-controlled.

goal: Present the best opportunities first with an auditable decision UI and concise operational digest.

items.instr:
Rank qualification, confidence, career fit, job quality, freshness, ROI, channel probability and effort.
Show why each job is ranked.
items.doneWhen: Queue prioritizes quality rather than raw volume.

items.instr:
Display decision, score, confidence, evidence, blockers, gaps, channel, CV strategy and learning factors.
Allow inspection of supporting information.
items.doneWhen: Operator can understand and challenge recommendations.

items.instr:
Include high-quality matches, prepared/awaiting approval/submitted items, failures, interviews, offers, rejections, follow-ups and learning changes.
Never expose credentials/secrets.
items.doneWhen: Digest is generated reliably.

goal: Connect outcomes back to future decisions with safety guardrails and a KPI dashboard.

items.instr:
Implement JOB → QUALIFICATION → APPLICATION → CHANNEL/CV/TEMPLATE → OUTCOME → LEARNING → UPDATED WEIGHTS → NEXT QUALIFICATION.
Existing process-learning.service.ts is not complete until it actually influences future behavior.
items.doneWhen: A controlled historical outcome measurably changes a future decision.

items.instr:
Prevent one-off overfitting, runaway weights, feedback loops, confidence inflation and contaminated outcomes.
Use bounded weights, minimum samples, rollback/versioning, audit history and frozen evaluation data.
items.doneWhen: Learning changes are bounded, explainable, reversible and regression-tested.

items.instr:
Track discovery, qualification, applications, duplicates, submission success, response, interview, offer and rejection rates.
Track channel/CV/template performance, confidence, false positives/negatives, near misses, effort and source outcomes.
Separate volume from quality metrics.
items.doneWhen: Dashboard demonstrates meaningful outcome improvement rather than merely increased application count.
